top news.title: Apple raises Mac, iPad, and other product prices by 15%-25%, saying it has “never seen a component price increase this much, this quickly”; iPhone is unchanged

tweets.author: @mkbhd
tweets.text: Memory price hikes have finally started hitting Apple. Today, they raised some base prices: Macbook Neo: $599 -> $699 Macbook Air: $1099 -> $1299 Macbook Pro: $1699 -> $1999 Mac Studio: $1999 -> $2499 iPad Air $599 - $749 iPad Pro: $999 -> $1199

tweets.author: @sensanders
tweets.text: Corporate greed is Tim Cook, the billionaire Apple CEO, claiming that hiking prices on Apple products by over $200 is “unavoidable” after it made $112 billion in profits last year & spent $310 billion on stock buybacks.  These price hikes aren't unavoidable.  They're unacceptable.

tweets.author: @elonmusk
tweets.text: Tim Cook, who told The Wall Street Journal that the jump in costs was unlike anything he had seen “in any area in over 40 years.” Biggest price jump in anything I've ever seen too.

sub_items.title: Apple says “the rapid expansion of AI data centers has created an extraordinary surge in demand for memory and storage”; the MacBook Neo rises from $599 to $699
Apple stock closed down 6.15% on Thursday after the company raised some product prices, its worst fall since April 2025

top news.title: Microsoft says the price of Xbox consoles will increase on August 1 by $100 for 512GB models and $150 for 1TB models, the third price increase since 2025

tweets.author: @zhugeex
tweets.text: The most important part of the announcement: “Unfortunately, console storage and memory prices have increased by more than 2.5x and we expect another doubling by the fall of 2027.”

tweets.author: @paultassi
tweets.text: You gotta be kidding me. Prices so high they don't even say them out loud and the 2TB model got so expensive they discontinued it entirely

tweets.author: @kalaelizabeth
tweets.text: Asha saying that gaming has become “too expensive for gamers” literally yesterday and then raising Xbox prices today lol

top news.title: IBM details a 0.7nm chip manufacturing process that utilizes a “nanostack” 3D transistor architecture, which it says could continue chip innovation for 10 years

tweets.author: @lithos_graphein
tweets.text: IBM's nanostack is a CFET device, but it uses wafer bonding instead of making them on 1 wafer. I have no idea how they'd get the alignment for this to work. [image]

tweets.author: @iancutress
tweets.text: OMG @IBM just announced its 0.7nm process node using homegrown NanoStack technology.  It defines a route for transistors after GAA by using a staggered CFET design enabling 50% logic scaling, 40% SRAM scaling, and 666 million transistors per sq mm***.

tweets.author: @kimmonismus
tweets.text: IBM says it can fit nearly 100 billion transistors onto a chip the size of a fingernail, almost 2x the density of its 2 nm chip from 2021.  • up to 50% more performance  • or 70% better energy efficiency  • 40% SRAM scaling for AI workloads Important caveat: this is still research, not a chip shipping tomorrow.  IBM says production could happen as early as the next 5 years.
